expertInsight: The part that needs real practice is identity resolution. Reading about match rules teaches you the words, but you only understand reconciliation once you have watched two source records merge and seen which value won. Build one small end-to-end setup: bring data in. Map it, resolve it. Build a segment, send it somewhere. Also learn where data spaces fit, because questions about keeping brands or regions apart come up more than people expect.

whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Data 360 Consultant exam?

personas.label: Data architects
personas.description: You design customer data models and connections and want to demonstrate how to build them in Data 360.

personas.label: CRM and data analysts
personas.description: You work with customer information across systems and want to validate your skills in unification and segmentation.

personas.label: Implementation consultants

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Data 360 Consultant exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers Data 360 concepts and workflows that differ from core Salesforce administration. Study how source data is ingested, mapped to the data model, unified through identity resolution, and used for segments and activations.
bullets: 60 scored questions plus a small number of unscored questions, in 105 minutes.
70% passing score. Confirm the current passing requirement in the official exam guide before scheduling.
Learn the terminology: Review data streams, data lake objects, data model objects, identity resolution, calculated insights, and activations.
Practice the workflow: Ingest and map data, resolve profiles, build a segment, and activate it.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build a complete flow in a trial org: bring data in, map it to the data model, resolve identities, create a segment, and activate that segment. Aim for at least 80% on practice sets and be ready to explain why records should or should not be unified.

examFormat.heading: Data 360 Consultant exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Questions focus on customer data workflows and their configuration.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe records arriving from several systems and ask how to unify them, or describe an audience need and ask how to build and send a segment to a destination.
bestWayToPass: Separate matching from reconciliation: Know how identity resolution determines which records refer to one person and how it chooses values when sources differ.
Map data yourself: Ingest sample data and map it to data model objects. Pay attention to keys and relationships.
Build segments and activations: Create an audience and send it to a destination, then review how membership refreshes.
Compare ingestion methods: Review batch and streaming ingestion, plus options that access data without copying it.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you bring customer data into Salesforce Data 360, model it, resolve it into one profile per person, then segment and activate it. Expect scenarios about matching records, mapping data and sending audiences to other systems. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 70% pass mark, weighted towards Data Activations and Utilization (20%) and Data Source Connection and Ingestion (18%).

blocks.heading: The Data 360 Workflow
blocks.body: A common workflow is to ingest source data, map it to the shared data model, resolve identities, create useful insights or segments, and activate results. Data streams connect to sources such as Salesforce, cloud storage, websites, or applications. Ingested data is stored in data lake objects (DLOs), then mapped to data model objects (DMOs) that represent concepts such as individuals or engagements. Identity resolution links records that refer to the same person. Segments select profiles that meet specified criteria, and activations send membership to a destination.

blocks.heading: Ingestion and Data Modeling
blocks.body: Data streams bring data into Data 360 through configured connectors or other supported ingestion methods. Data lake objects retain ingested source data. Mapping aligns fields and records with data model objects, which provide a consistent structure for using data across sources. Keys and relationships matter because they determine how records connect. Learn which ingestion method and mapping approach fit the source and the freshness requirement.

blocks.heading: Identity Resolution and Unified Profiles
blocks.body: Identity resolution applies match rules to determine which source records refer to the same individual. Reconciliation rules determine which source value is used for a field when records are unified. The resulting unified profile brings together information from linked records. Matching and reconciliation solve different problems: matching decides whether records belong together, while reconciliation selects the value displayed for a field.

blocks.heading: Calculated Insights, Segments, and Activations
blocks.body: Calculated insights create derived measures from Data 360 data, such as purchase totals or days since a customer’s last activity. A segment selects profiles that meet criteria and can be refreshed according to its configuration. An activation publishes segment membership to a destination, such as a marketing platform or another connected system. Understand how source data, unified profiles, calculated insights, and segments support a downstream audience.

blocks.heading: Consent, Governance, and Data Actions
blocks.body: Data 360 supports consent and privacy requirements through the configured consent data and privacy attributes. Implementations must use those controls to honor applicable preferences and requests. Data actions can respond to configured changes, such as segment membership, and initiate downstream work. Consider data governance, destination behavior, and refresh timing when designing an activation.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Data 360 Consultant exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each scenario, identify the step involved: source connection, data mapping, identity resolution, segment creation, or activation. Then choose the feature that performs that step.

blocks.heading: Know the Identity Resolution Steps
blocks.body: Match rules determine whether records belong to the same individual. Reconciliation rules choose the surviving field values. Practice both decisions with records from multiple sources.

blocks.heading: Map a Source to the Data Model
blocks.body: Ingest sample records and map their fields to suitable data model objects. Check identifiers and relationships so records can be connected correctly.

blocks.heading: Build and Activate an Audience
blocks.body: Create a segment from profile criteria, then select a destination and activation settings. Understand how segment refresh affects when the audience changes.

blocks.heading: Compare Ingestion Options
blocks.body: Review batch and streaming options and the cases where data can be accessed without being copied. Choose based on source capability and freshness needs.

blocks.heading: Apply Consent and Governance
blocks.body: Understand how consent and privacy attributes inform profile use and activation. Make sure downstream destinations respect the configured requirements.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials after the Data 360 Consultant exam
nextCertsAfter.intro: Continue with a Salesforce platform credential or a related analytics and data specialization.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the main purpose of Data 360?
options: A pricing tool for enterprise contracts
Unify customer data into profiles
A backup store for Salesforce data
A batch email marketing system
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data 360 brings customer data together from different sources so it can be understood and used across the business.
whyWrong: CPQ configures products and pricing; it is not the main purpose of Data 360.
Data 360 is not limited to backup storage.
Email delivery is one possible downstream use, not the platform’s overall purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a data stream in Data 360?
options: A live sales dashboard that streams current results
A Marketing Cloud journey started by a segment
An Apex export job that sends data to a warehouse
A source connection that brings data into Data 360
sampleQuestions.explanation: A data stream connects Data 360 to a source and brings that source data into the platform.
whyWrong: A dashboard displays analytics rather than ingesting source records.
A journey may use activated data but is not a Data 360 data stream.
An export job sends data out rather than configuring a source ingestion.

sampleQuestions.question: What are Data Model Objects (DMOs)?
options: Remote SOAP external objects
CRM Analytics report types
Custom Lead fields that store source system metadata
Standardized structures for business data
sampleQuestions.explanation: DMOs provide a standardized structure for representing data such as individuals and engagements.
whyWrong: External objects expose external data and are not the shared Data 360 model described here.
Report types are used for Salesforce reporting, not to model ingested Data 360 data.
DMOs are broader modeled structures, not a set of Lead metadata fields.

sampleQuestions.question: What does identity resolution do?
options: Checks privacy consent before ingestion
Assigns Salesforce IDs to profiles
Match records into a unified profile
Authenticates source APIs with OAuth
sampleQuestions.explanation: Identity resolution uses configured matching logic to determine which records represent the same person and combine them in a unified profile.
whyWrong: Consent handling is important but is separate from determining whether records match.
Record ID assignment is not the purpose of identity resolution.
OAuth authenticates connections; it does not link customer records.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a unified profile?
options: A Person Account that replaces duplicate Contacts
A consolidated view of a person built from linked source records
A report type listing interactions for an Account
A Marketing Cloud subscriber record enriched with CRM data
sampleQuestions.explanation: A unified profile brings together information from source records that identity resolution has linked to the same individual.
whyWrong: A unified profile is not necessarily a single Salesforce Person Account record.
A report type is a reporting construct, not a profile created from resolution.
A subscriber record may be a source or destination record but is not the unified profile itself.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Data 360 segment?
options: A Marketing Cloud list used only for subscription preferences
A criteria-based audience of unified profiles
A scheduled export to a business intelligence platform
A permission set group for Data 360 users
sampleQuestions.explanation: A segment selects unified profiles that satisfy configured criteria for analysis or activation.
whyWrong: Subscription preferences are separate from defining an audience of profiles.
An export may deliver segment data but is not the segment itself.
Permission sets control user access and do not define customer audiences.

sampleQuestions.question: What does activation do in Data 360?
options: Runs identity resolution rules on each newly ingested data stream
Gives users access to edit segments
Publishes segment membership to a connected destination
Turns on Data 360 in Salesforce Setup
sampleQuestions.explanation: Activation sends a segment and its membership to a configured destination for downstream use.
whyWrong: Identity resolution creates unified profiles before segment activation.
User permissions are managed separately from sending segment data.
Enabling the product is not the same as publishing a segment to a destination.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a calculated insight?
options: A Salesforce metric updated by Apex
A metric derived from Data 360 data
An Einstein score stored in a formula field
A dashboard widget showing segment counts
sampleQuestions.explanation: A calculated insight derives a metric from Data 360 data, such as purchase value or recency.
whyWrong: A calculated insight is a Data 360 measure, not a metric maintained by a custom Apex job.
Prediction scores and calculated insights are different types of outputs.
A widget may display an insight but is not the insight definition itself.

sampleQuestions.question: Which approach supports consent and privacy handling in Data 360?
options: Shield encryption keys that hide fields
A daily synced Marketing Cloud opt-out
Configured consent and privacy attributes
Manual deletion by an administrator
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data 360 can use consent data and privacy attributes to support configured opt-out and deletion handling across ingested customer data.
whyWrong: Encryption protects data but does not by itself record a person’s consent choices.
A single email field does not cover all consent and privacy information across sources.
Manual deletion alone does not provide a scalable configured privacy process.

sampleQuestions.question: What work may a Data 360 Consultant perform on an implementation?
options: Manage org sharing and Data 360 user permissions
Write Apex triggers for all platform event ingestion
Plan a Data 360 implementation
Create marketing emails from activated segments
sampleQuestions.explanation: A consultant helps design and configure the end-to-end data workflow, including ingestion, unification, activation, and governance.
whyWrong: User and record access can be part of the project, but it does not describe the full consulting role.
Custom Apex is not the only or default way to ingest source data into Data 360.
Email campaign creation is a downstream marketing task rather than the full consulting scope.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Data Action used for?
options: A validation rule for malformed records
A Flow after every ingestion job
A batch export to an external data lake
An event trigger for downstream work
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Actions can respond to configured events such as a change in segment membership and start downstream processes.
whyWrong: Validation and data quality rules serve a different purpose.
Data Actions are not simply a Flow for every completed ingestion job.
An export moves data in batches and is different from event-based downstream action.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Data 360 differ from a traditional data warehouse?
options: Requires all data to be transformed before ingestion
Stores data only in relational tables
Cannot handle structured customer records
A scheduled snapshot of prepared customer data
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data 360 is designed to unify customer data and make it available for segmentation, activation, and Salesforce use.
whyWrong: Data 360 includes ingestion and transformation capabilities; external preprocessing is not always required.
This description overlooks Data 360 data model and activation capabilities.
Data 360 supports structured customer data as well as the features described in the question.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Data 360 object represents the unified person across source systems?
options: Account
Segment
Contact Point Email
Individual
sampleQuestions.explanation: Individual is the data model object representing a person; a unified profile can combine linked information about that person.
whyWrong: Accounts represent organizations or customer accounts, not the person object asked for.
A segment is a group of profiles selected by criteria.
Contact Point Email represents an email address, not the person.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a Data 360 data stream?
options: Create activation destinations
Run calculated insights
Ingest source data for mapping
Export completed segments
sampleQuestions.explanation: A data stream connects to a source and ingests records that can then be mapped to the data model.
whyWrong: Destinations are configured for activation, after the data preparation and segmentation steps.
Calculated insights derive measures from data already ingested.
Exporting segments is activation rather than source ingestion.

sampleQuestions.question: How can Data 360 support Einstein and Agentforce?
options: Supports Marketing Cloud journeys but no AI features
Provides unified customer context for AI
Only supports batch data exports
Does not support AI use cases
sampleQuestions.explanation: Unified profiles can provide a consolidated customer context for supported Einstein and Agentforce use cases.
whyWrong: Data 360 use is not limited to Marketing Cloud.
This describes how unified data can support AI grounding and context.
AI use is not limited to batch exports.

sampleQuestions.question: A company has separate business units that each need their own isolated Data 360 data, with no accidental overlap between them. What should a consultant configure?
options: Data spaces
A single shared dataset for everyone
A permission set with no restrictions
A Marketing Cloud business unit only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data spaces are organizational containers in Data 360 that isolate data, letting separate business units keep their data apart within the same org.
whyWrong: A single shared dataset is exactly what the company wants to avoid.
An unrestricted permission set controls access broadly, it doesn't create data isolation by business unit.
A Marketing Cloud business unit manages Marketing Cloud, not Data 360 data isolation.

sampleQuestions.question: Two incoming records both have the email field populated, but with slightly different spellings of the customer's name. Which type of matching rule is designed to catch this as a likely match?
options: A fuzzy match rule on name + address
An exact match rule on email only
No rule can catch this
A rule based on record creation date
sampleQuestions.explanation: Fuzzy matching is designed to catch records that are likely the same person despite small variations, like a misspelled name, by matching on a combination of attributes rather than requiring an exact string match.
whyWrong: An exact match rule on email would actually work here too if emails matched exactly, but the question is about handling near-miss name spelling, which is what fuzzy matching is for.
Fuzzy matching exists specifically to catch cases like this.
Record creation date has nothing to do with identifying the same real-world person.

sampleQuestions.question: A consultant needs to calculate each customer's total spend over the last 90 days from Data Model Object data. What's used to build that metric?
options: A Calculated Insight, written as a SQL query against DMOs
A Data Action triggered by a change in a Data Model Object
A Data Space
An Activation Target
sampleQuestions.explanation: Calculated Insights are SQL-based metrics computed over DMO data, exactly the kind of aggregation needed for a rolling spend total.
whyWrong: A Data Action triggers an event based on a condition, it doesn't compute an aggregated metric.
A Data Space isolates data, it doesn't calculate anything.
An Activation Target is a destination for a segment, not a calculation mechanism.

sampleQuestions.question: A client asks whether they should use Data 360 or a narrower, already-existing Salesforce feature to solve a straightforward reporting need. What should the consultant do first?
options: Scope the actual business requirement and recommend the right-sized tool, not default to the newest platform
Recommend Data 360 for every reporting need, because it is the newest and broadest Salesforce data platform
Tell the client it's impossible without more licenses
Build the solution before discussing requirements
sampleQuestions.explanation: Solution Positioning is about matching the actual requirement to the right capability, sometimes that's Data 360, and sometimes an existing, simpler Salesforce feature already covers it.
whyWrong: Defaulting to Data 360 regardless of fit is the opposite of good solution positioning.
Jumping to "it's impossible" without scoping the requirement isn't a real assessment.
Building before understanding the requirement risks solving the wrong problem.

sampleQuestions.question: A marketing user should be able to view Data 360 segments and insights, but not change ingestion or admin settings. Which permission set fits?
options: Data 360 Marketing Viewer
Data 360 Admin
A blank profile with no permission set
System Administrator
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Marketing Viewer-style permission set gives read access to segments and insights without granting the broader admin and ingestion configuration rights that a Data 360 Admin permission set would include.
whyWrong: Data 360 Admin grants configuration access well beyond what this user needs.
A blank profile with no permission set would leave the user without even the viewing access required.
System Administrator is far broader access than the scenario calls for, and isn't the Data 360-specific answer.
